criteria: Open C mutes string 6; strings 3 and 1 are open; sounding notes C, E, G, C, E. Preserve low-to-high fixture order and check service-array order separately.
Ascending DifficultyScore ranks returned candidates only. Hypothetical scores are not fixture or captured query results.
Choosing a voicing still needs clean intended notes, an actual fingering, comfort and musical context; no playing outcome has been observed.
A-form span 5 - 3 = 2 and E-form span 10 - 8 = 2; equal fret counts do not prove equal millimeters or effort.
For the exact teaching arrays: A-form BarreRequired=true, E-form=false; IsFullBarre=false for both. These predicates answer different questions.
The claim is conditional on the generator returning that array. Real fingering, hand comfort, fresh service output and musician review remain separate.
A MIDI 52/59 and B 54/61 give interval classes 7/7; both notes move +2, so one source-predicted Fifths issue and IsClean=false.
A-to-C has opposite directions and final interval 3; clean report does not make C an interchangeable harmony or better music.
A-to-D shares only string 4 and yields no checked pair. The code misses cross-string voice continuity; ten-attempt playing target remains proposed.
Default high-to-low indexing gives E, C, G, E, C, G. Five labels match; string 5 fret 3 is G, not the source marker C. This is a historical source finding.
showStringLabels hides tuning labels, not populated marker labels. A note-reveal task is not an existing tested feature.
Coordinate-only callback lacks pre-feedback note prediction, verified key and cue/feedback timing. A synthetic corrected answer is not observed learning.
Four correct out of 6; losses total 1.52 and mean 0.2533 rounded. The sixth wrong answer contributes 0.81. All rows are synthetic.

A real next-day held-out comparison must lower Brier without reducing accuracy under the guardrail. No real intervention or learner measurement exists.
Low-to-high strings 6 to 1 are D, A, D, G, A, D; strings 6, 2, 1 drop 2 semitones from standard tuning.
Open collections are D, G, A versus D, F#, A for Open D; string 3 drops 1 semitone. These are tuning/harmonic statements, not cultural authenticity.
Lookup confidence 1.0 is assigned by source formatting. It does not validate uncited cultural prose or prove live chatbot routing.
